title: Tonkotsu Ramen
subtitle: rich milky pork bone broth with noodles
excerpt: Tonkotsu ramen is a rich, cloudy pork broth made by boiling bones at a hard rolling boil for several hours. The result is a deeply savoury, milky-white soup served over thin noodles with soft-boiled egg and pork. It takes time but the effort pays off.
sourceNotes: Tonkotsu ramen originated in Kurume, Fukuoka prefecture, in 1937. The cloudy pork-bone broth is achieved by boiling bones at a hard rolling boil for several hours. It spread across Japan and became one of the country's most celebrated regional dishes.

content.text: Tonkotsu ramen is one of Japan's great comfort dishes. The broth needs a hard boil -- not a gentle simmer -- to turn milky white and extract the collagen from the bones. Plan for 3 to 4 hours of cooking time. The result is worth it.

items.prepNote: use pork bones or pork shoulder for a rich broth
use as base -- top up with water as needed
use chashu pork belly if available -- simmer in soy sauce and mirin
use soy sauce -- for seasoning the broth

content.text: Blanch the pork shoulder in boiling water for 5 minutes. Drain and rinse under cold water. This removes impurities and keeps the broth clean.

Place the pork, garlic, ginger, and chicken stock in a large saucepan. Bring to a hard rolling boil. Boil uncovered for 3 to 4 hours, topping up with water to keep the bones submerged. The broth should turn milky white.
While the broth cooks, soft-boil the eggs for 6 minutes. Transfer to cold water. Peel and set aside.
Cook the streaky bacon (or chashu pork) in a hot frying pan until caramelised. Set aside.
Cook the noodles according to the packet instructions. Drain and divide between 4 deep bowls.
Strain the broth through a colander. Season with soy sauce and salt. Ladle over the noodles. Top with sliced pork, a halved soft-boiled egg, and spring onion.

items.symptom: Broth is thin and clear, not milky
items.cause: Not boiling hard enough -- tonkotsu needs a vigorous rolling boil
items.fix: Increase the heat and boil uncovered at a full rolling boil for the full 3--4 hours. A gentle simmer will not emulsify the fat.

content.text: Tonkotsu ramen comes from Fukuoka, on the southern island of Kyushu. Local shops keep their broth going for days, topping it up as it reduces. The noodles are thin and firm. Toppings vary by shop. This is a dish that rewards patience.
